title: Cone-beam computed tomography in endodontics: patient perceptions, outcomes, and radiation awareness
html: BACKGROUND: The impact of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) on patient-reported outcome measures in endodontics remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to identify patients' perceived values in diagnostic imaging, investigate the impact of CBCT vs periapical radiography (PR), and assess patient knowledge of ionizing radiation. METHODS: tests (P < .05). RESULTS: Baseline radiation knowledge was limited, with 59% of participants rating their understanding as poor or very poor. Despite this, patients prioritized diagnostic accuracy over a low radiation dose. The inclusion of CBCT considerably improved patient-reported outcome measures. Overall, 79.5% of participants considered CBCT more useful and helpful than PR, 60.7% reported increased confidence in their treatment plans, and 59.0% reported greater trust in clinicians compared with PR alone. Most participants (89.7%) indicated that they would undergo CBCT for future care if clinically indicated. CONCLUSIONS: Patients perceived CBCT as superior to PR for understanding their diagnosis and for building confidence in the treatment plan, despite having limited knowledge of ionizing radiation. This suggests that patients perceive the diagnostic benefits of CBCT as outweighing its risks. PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: CBCT may enhance patient confidence beyond diagnostics. Clinicians should explain CBCT's diagnostic advantages and radiation risks and enhance the personalized consent process to address gaps in patients' limited knowledge of ionizing radiation.
